short: The Allied powers and Germany signed the agreement that ended combat operations in the First World War.
full:
At 5:00 a.m. on 11 November 1918, German representatives and Supreme Allied Commander Ferdinand Foch signed an armistice in a railway carriage in the Forest of Compiègne. Facing domestic revolution, exhausted militaries, and the collapse of their allies, the German high command accepted terms that amounted to near-total demilitarization and withdrawal.

Fighting continued until the agreement came into effect at 11:00 a.m., resulting in thousands of final-day casualties. The Armistice halted the bloodshed on the Western Front and paved the way for the Treaty of Versailles the following year. It marked the definitive defeat of the German Empire and the end of the four-year global catastrophe.
